text_simplified: The text discusses the rights of children in Islam and emphasizes the importance of justice, truthfulness, and mercy in the tarbiyah (upbringing) of children. It also clarifies that children have rights such as love, respect, healthcare, and education. Parents must teach their children Islamic values and good akhlaq (manners).

review_defects.why: The Arabic 'الأخلاق الحميدة' means 'good morals/character', which is broader than 'manners'. The parenthetical 'manners' narrows the meaning to etiquette, potentially losing the moral dimension.
